title: Why Donald Trump won in 2024
gist: Noah Smith re-ups his four-part 2024 election post-mortem amid a failing second Trump term: Democrats lost because identity politics alienated upwardly mobile Hispanic voters, the 2021-22 inflation (worsened by the American Rescue Plan) angered voters more than unemployment would have, the educated professional class grew disconnected from non-college America, and blue cities failed on housing, costs and disorder.

insights.claim: Smith writes that Trump's second presidency is widely seen as a failure on inflation, the Iran War, corruption and racial harmony, with his approval rating drifting steadily lower.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Weak presidential approval raises odds of divided government and policy gridlock after the midterms.
insights.quote: Everyone except the die-hard faithful now realizes that Donald Trump’s second presidency is a colossal failure.
insights.locator: Everyone except the die-hard faithful

insights.claim: Smith predicts Trump will probably lose the midterms and become a lame duck issuing grandiose, unworkable executive orders while facing Congressional investigations.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A Democratic midterm win would shift policy influence and raise executive-order-driven volatility.
insights.quote: Trump will probably lose the midterms, and become a lame duck president
insights.locator: Trump will probably lose the midterms

insights.claim: Trump's promise to give every American $5000 for voting Republican backfired, and his symbolic controversies (e.g., renaming AI 'artificial superintelligence') aim to activate negative polarization.
